chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) said:
I asked him about a man who sees blood on his brother's garment while he is praying; he said, 'It does not harm him until he departs.'
ai.seo_question: Does blood on clothing invalidate the prayer in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the ruling of *al-ghhaflah* (negligence) regarding minor impurity, specifically blood, on clothing during prayer. It establishes that the presence of such impurity does not invalidate the prayer or cause spiritual harm to the worshipper, provided they are unaware or do not actively remove it before concluding the prayer. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of ease (*taysir*) in worship, distinguishing between major impurities that require immediate removal and minor ones that are excused under certain conditions.
